hypothesis: The kernel is honest only if it also stays silent: a pattern whose lens the surface cannot express (Flyweight identity), a procedurally-shaped CRUD model with no pattern and no equations, and a pattern-lookalike with a legitimately differing path must not produce fabricated findings, while a scripted conventional test still catches the seeded defect. The near-floor control proves the apparatus can see a real violation and name it identically to the conventional arm.
comparison_rule: unique = probe_elements - baseline_elements; an element is the named witness listed per fault. Both arms name elements in the same vocabulary; a finding counts only when its mapped element is in the pre-registered set. A probe finding outside the set is a fabricated finding and fails the bundle.

control.lens: source x current = cached (the cache holds its source's current value)
control.gap: one declared value equality only; cache population, eviction, expiry, and concurrent refresh have no representation

flyweight.lens: client -> key -> factory and client -> flyweight name one shared instance; handle and intrinsic values are equal data
flyweight.gap: object identity / share count has no predicate in the kernel surface; the duplicate row carries equal handle and intrinsic values, so every expressible value equation passes and the duplicate is invisible (0 findings)

crud.lens: none — a procedurally-shaped CRUD snapshot with no pattern and no equations
crud.gap: read-after-write consistency is procedural/temporal and has no path-equation form; with no equations there is nothing for check to evaluate, so silence is correct, not a missed check

lookalike.lens: charged = list x discount (the declared transformation); the naive decorator delegation lens charged = list is the over-reporting claim
lookalike.gap: the kernel cannot distinguish an intended difference from a defect except through declared arrows and equations; check has no underconstraint detector, so a wrongly omitted equation is invisible
